title: Finite limits and subcanonical finite-cover topology on profinite action spaces
statement:
Work in compatible universes and small skeletons [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, let $P$ be the profinite site with finite jointly surjective covers [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $P_J$ have profinite continuous left $J$-spaces, continuous equivariant maps and finite jointly surjective covers [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $H(S)=J\times S$ with left translation on $J$, and $tS=S$ with trivial action [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters]. The category $P_J$ is small and has finite limits created by the forgetful functor to profinite spaces: its terminal object is the one-point trivial action, its products carry diagonal actions, and its equalizers carry restricted actions. Its finite jointly surjective families form a pretopology stable under pullback and finite indexed composition, including the empty covering of the empty object. This topology is subcanonical. More explicitly, for any finite cover $\{T_i\to T\}$ and any $U\in P_J$, restriction is a bijection
$$C_J(T,U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Eq}\left(\prod_i C_J(T_i,U)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}C_J(T_i\times_TT_j,U)\right),$$
where $C_J$ denotes continuous equivariant maps. The same assertion for continuous maps holds on $P$. The trivial-action functor $t:P\to P_J$ preserves finite limits and covering families.

proof.text: Use the universe bound and skeleton of [def-weil-size-convention]. The collection of smaller-universe profinite spaces, their action maps and their continuous equivariant morphisms is a set in the larger universe, so the chosen category is small there. First form limits without actions. The point is terminal. For any profinite span, [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product] states that the set-theoretic fibre product with its subspace topology is profinite. A map to this subspace is continuous precisely when its two coordinates are continuous, so the usual pair of maps gives its pullback universal property. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks](1) gives all finite limits in $P$.

proof.text: Let $F:I\to P_J$ be any finite diagram and $(L,p_i)$ any limit cone of its underlying profinite diagram, as constructed in step 1. By [lem-sfb-profinite-topological-limits] it is also a limit of topological spaces, even for test spaces which are not profinite. The continuous maps $J\times L\to F(i)$, $(g,x)\mapsto g\cdot p_i(x)$, are compatible because every diagram arrow is equivariant. Apply that topological universal property with $W=J\times L$ to obtain a unique continuous action map $a:J\times L\to L$. For the unit, both $a(1,-)$ and the identity have the same composites with every $p_i$; for multiplication, both $a(g,a(h,-))$ and $a(gh,-)$ have the same composites, so limit uniqueness gives the action laws. For an equivariant cone from $Q$, its underlying mediating map $b:Q\to L$ satisfies $p_i(b(gq))=g\cdot p_i(b(q))$ for every $i$, hence is equivariant by the same uniqueness. Consequently this is a limit cone in $P_J$. The displayed coordinate equations also force the action uniquely for any lift of the underlying cone, proving creation of finite limits. For the empty diagram the same construction gives the unique action on the point.

proof.text: These limits have the asserted forms. The terminal point has the trivial action, and on a product the coordinate equations in step 2 say $g\cdot(x,y)=(g\cdot x,g\cdot y)$. For parallel equivariant maps $f,h:X\to Y$, form the pullback of $(f,h):X\to Y\times Y$ and the diagonal $Y\to Y\times Y$. Its underlying space identifies with $E=\{x:f(x)=h(x)\}$ with the subspace topology: the inverse maps are $x\mapsto(x,f(x))$ and the first projection, both continuous. The restricted action is defined since $f(gx)=g f(x)=g h(x)=h(gx)$ for $x\in E$. The equalizer universal property is the unique factorization of a map whose image lies in $E$.

proof.text: Check the covering axioms of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) pointwise. An isomorphism is surjective. If $\{T_i\to T\}$ is jointly surjective and $V\to T$ is equivariant, each $v\in V$ has a lift $x\in T_i$ of its image, so $(x,v)\in T_i\times_TV$ lifts $v$. The pullbacks are those of steps 1–2. If each $\{T_{ij}\to T_i\}$ also covers, lift a point of $T$ first to some $T_i$ and then to some $T_{ij}$; the composite family is jointly surjective. A finite family of finite index sets has finite union. Reindexing a covering family along a bijection does not change the underlying jointly-surjective condition. The empty family is jointly surjective exactly when its target is empty, and its pullback or indexed composite remains an empty cover of the empty target. These checks apply with actions omitted as well.

proof.text: Let $\{q_i:T_i\to T\}$ be a finite cover and let continuous maps $f_i:T_i\to U$ agree on every $T_i\times_TT_j$. Put $D=\coprod_i T_i$ with its disjoint-union topology and let $q:D\to T$ be induced by the $q_i$. The space $D$ is compact: restrict an open cover to each component, take its finite subcover, and unite these finitely many finite lists. The map $q$ is continuous and onto, and $T$ is Hausdorff. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient] with whole-space subsets to conclude that $q$ is quotient. For $t\in T$, define $f(t)=f_i(x)$ for any lift $q_i(x)=t$; overlap agreement makes this independent of both $i$ and $x$. For an open subset $O\subseteq U$, the inverse image $q^{-1}(f^{-1}O)$ is open, since its intersection with component $T_i$ is $f_i^{-1}O$. The quotient criterion implies $f^{-1}O$ is open, proving continuity. Surjectivity forces uniqueness of $f$. This proves the claimed equalizer bijection for continuous maps on $P$, including empty $D$ and $T$.

proof.text: For equivariant $q_i$ and $f_i$ in step 5, the descended map is equivariant: given $g\in J$ and a lift $x\in T_i$ of $t$, the point $gx$ lifts $gt$, and $f(gt)=f_i(gx)=g f_i(x)=g f(t)$. Conversely, restrictions of a continuous equivariant map agree on overlaps. Thus restriction gives exactly the displayed equalizer bijection for $C_J(-,U)$. By the sheaf criterion of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), every representable on $P_J$ is a sheaf; equivalently the generated topology is subcanonical. The criterion applies to the pretopology checked in step 4. Step 5 gives the same conclusion on $P$. For the empty cover of the empty space, the set of maps out of the empty space and both empty products are singletons, as required.

proof.text: The functor $t$ of [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters] retains each underlying space and map. It sends the point to the terminal trivial action and sends a profinite pullback to its underlying pullback with trivial action: the diagonal action on trivial factors is trivial. These are the terminal object and pullbacks constructed in steps 1–3, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks](2) implies that $t$ preserves finite limits. Since its underlying maps do not change, a finite jointly surjective family remains one, including the empty family over the empty space. Hence $t$ also preserves covering families.
